Subject: Re: Draft Order Form (pricing slabs + tax)

Hi Monica —

Thanks for sending the updated order form. We reviewed the commercial sections with finance and procurement and have a few redlines we need to get aligned on before legal will sign:

1) Pricing slabs: We need the PO to allow quarterly slab true-ups rather than monthly invoices. Our usage is bursty; quarterly reconciliation simplifies our internal chargeback. Can Redwood accept quarterly invoicing with pro-rated mid-quarter adjustments?
2) Minimums & credits: The current Minimum Commitment (Section 2) is expressed as an annual token commitment with monthly invoicing. We prefer a tiered slab (Q1: 0-500k tokens @ $0.0035, Q2: 500k-2M @ $0.0029, etc.) and a credit mechanism for unused tokens at quarter end.
3) Net terms: We need Net45 for this customer (enterprise standard). Net30 is difficult for our procurement cycle.
4) Taxes: Please confirm Redwood will not gross-up fees and that AstraData is responsible for local VAT/GST where applicable; we will provide tax-exempt certificates where appropriate. If Redwood requires tax in the island jurisdictions, please call out the list.
5) PO flow: Procurement requires that invoices reference PO# AST-78932 and that Redwood accepts emailed PDF POs attached to invoices.

We attached a marked-up PDF with inline comments (see attachment). Can you route this to your legal and finance leads and let us know which of the above Redwood can accept as-is vs. needs alternative language?

Thanks,
Samira Khan
Head of Vendor Management
AstraData Inc.

Hi Samira / Monica —

Thanks for the markup. I reviewed the redlines with Karthik (pricing) and Lauren (finance). Below are proposed legal edits and open questions. I've included inline language suggestions you can paste into the order form.

1) Quarterly Invoicing + True-up:
Proposed language: "Invoices will be issued quarterly in arrears. Redwood will provide a usage statement at the end of each calendar quarter. If actual usage exceeds the invoiced slab, Redwood will invoice for the incremental usage at the applicable slab rate and payment will be due within the agreed payment term. If actual usage is below the slab, unused tokens will be credited to the customer's account as a one-time credit to be applied against the next quarter's invoice."
Open question: Does AstraData require the credit to be refundable in cash or is an account credit acceptable?

2) Tiered slab pricing and minimums:
Proposed language: "Order Forms may define pricing slabs by token bands and associated per-token rates. Annual minimum commitment remains in place; however, customers and Redwood may elect slab billing in lieu of fixed monthly draws. Slab breakpoints and associated credits will be specified in the applicable Order Form schedule."
Open question for Pricing: Karthik — does Redwood accept the proposed breakpoint at 500k for transition to the next slab? If not, suggest alternatives.

3) Net terms:
Proposed language: "Unless otherwise specified in the Order Form, invoices are due Net30. For Order Forms with committed capacity greater than $250k ARR, Customer may request Net45 terms subject to Redwood credit approval."
Aditya note: This preserves Redwood's default while allowing AstraData's ask if they meet the commit threshold or credit check.

4) Taxes:
Proposed language: "Fees are exclusive of applicable taxes. Customer will be responsible for any VAT/GST or other sales taxes unless Customer provides a valid exemption certificate, in which case Redwood will not charge tax for the exempted jurisdictions. Redwood will provide tax invoices where required by local law."
Open question: If AstraData requires Redwood to register in a jurisdiction, that is a separate commercial ask we need to escalate to finance/ops.

5) PO & invoicing references:
Proposed language: "Customer shall provide a purchase order number which must be referenced on all invoices. Redwood will accept emailed PDF purchase orders and will reference the PO number on invoice line items."

Please reply to confirm (a) cash refund vs. credit preference for unused tokens, (b) acceptance of proposed Net45 credit-threshold approach, and (c) whether AstraData expects Redwood to be tax-registered in any new jurisdictions. Happy to schedule a 30-min call if helpful.

—Aditya Rao
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai

Aditya / Monica —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and proposed language. Confirming AstraData's positions so we can finalize: 

1) Unused token refunds: AstraData prefers account credits (non-cash); cash refunds are not required.
2) Net terms: Net45 accepted under the condition that our initial committed purchase meets $300k ARR — we are comfortable with Redwood's credit check.
3) Taxes: AstraData will provide tax-exempt certificates for the US and EU entities where applicable. We do NOT require Redwood to register in additional jurisdictions at signing.

With those confirmations, we've updated the Order Form PDF and initiated the signature through DocuSign.
